refresh_rate: If > 0, then it is the Hz of the connection signal. Otherwise it is 1e12 Hz
defaults to 1e12 Hz, or effectively as fast as the main loop
number_of_values: integer that is greater than 0. Determines the number of values to send/receive by the connection
verbose: whether or not the connection should print the values to the screen whenever it sends/receives
port_ID: required if channel_type is udp, otherwise ignored
integer of the udp port number. Must be a valid port number
double_precision: optional if channel_type is udp, otherwise ignored
Determines whether to send/receive the udp message as single precision floats or double precision floats. This must match with the corresponding application for the message transfer to succeed
IP_address: optional if channel_type is udp, otherwise ignored
defaults to the local computer, '127.0.0.1', if type is send and all traffic, '0.0.0.0', if type is receive
determines where to send the udp message
wait_for_data: optional if channel_type is udp and type is receive, otherwise ignored

determines whether the udp receive command should block code execution until the message is received or whether to keep running even though a new message has not been received, in which case, the latest results are still used
little_endian: optional if channel_type is udp, otherwise ignored
determines the endian format type of the data within the udp message. True is little endian and False is big endian. Most current systems/applications use little endian
filename: required if channel_type is file, otherwise ignored
string that is the name of the file
if type is send, the file will be overwritten, if it is receive, the file will be read in as a database

database should be a csv formatted file, with a column header and the first column is time and the remaining columns are the values to be received from the database. recv commands should pass in the current time, and the database will be interpolated and return the remaining values
pathname: optional if channel_type is file, otherwise ignored
string of the path to the file
defaults to nothing, meaning that either the filename must contain the path, or the file must be in the same folder as the code
database_type: required if channel_type is file and type is receive, otherwise ignored
currently it must be 'rectilinear', but future versions of the code will allow other types of databases
